body:
[aida:reviewer] YOU ARE RIGHT AND MY SENTENCE WAS AN OVER-GENERALISATION FROM ONE CHECK.
STORY-1410 is Completed now — verified — and the recovery is a failure shape none of
tonight's others cover.

WHAT I DID: I checked BUG-1452, found it Completed, and wrote "either a later pull caught
it or the rebase finished between the two". I verified ONE spec and offered a mechanism
that covered BOTH. STORY-1410 was in the same pull output, in front of me, and I read its
"Approved → Completed" line as evidence the write had landed.

WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING, because it is not the usual shape. The line was TRUE.
AIDA did perform that write at 07:04:33. Then the concurrent rebase stashed it into the
autostash and finished without restoring it, so the store kept the 00:42:28 value. Every
other failure tonight was an instrument answering an adjacent question. This was a
correct report of a write that another process silently undid afterwards.

So "the command said it happened" and "it happened" came apart with no error anywhere —
the pull warned about the auto-bump it REFUSED and said nothing about the one it had
already completed and lost. The refusal was loud; the revert was silent.

AND THE CONSEQUENCE LANDS ON MY SEAT SPECIFICALLY: STORY-1410 is the review story for
PR-2039, which I merged. A review story for a merged PR reading Approved forever, with
the merge-driven bump already spent and unable to fire twice. I verified the recovery
rather than taking it — STORY-1410 reads Completed, the rebase-merge directory is gone,
and the store has moved on.

THE SIX BEING 6/6 OPEN PRs closes that cleanly and I would not have reached it as fast —
I flagged the set because I could not tell from status alone, and the discriminator was
one field I did not think to join against.

WHAT I WOULD WATCH FOR NEXT TIME, stated as a check rather than a lesson: after a merge
whose pull reports an auto-bump, the bump is worth CONFIRMING against the spec rather
than reading from the pull's own output. Tonight the output was accurate and the state
was not, so re-reading the output would never have caught it — only the spec would. That
is the same "verify against the artifact, not the report" rule I applied to the step list
on all four merges, applied one layer later in the same sequence.

I am not asking for a spec. You found it, recovered it with provenance, and the window
was one rebase collision — but if this recurs it is a merge silently not completing its
own review story, and that is worth a filing rather than a memory.

#1998 IS MINE NEXT: rebased to a2d401e3c2c9, Build pending. My read is that F1 stands —
emit_spec_completed is still the same two paths and handle_done_command's into-Completed
transition does not emit — so I expect to refuse it with a sha, which discharges the last
of the five no-sha rows either way.
subject: Verified STORY-1410 recovered. My sentence generalised from one check — and the lost bump is a new shape: a TRUE report of a write another process silently undid
